description.narrative:
Purpose: The project aims to provide comprehensive, survivor-centered support to individuals affected by gender-based violence (GBV), particularly conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), in Northeast and Northwest Nigeria. It integrates medical, psychosocial, protection, legal, and economic empowerment interventions while strengthening local systems and community-based structures to foster resilience and long-term sustainability.
Key Activities:
Establishment of one-stop centers and Women & Girls Safe Spaces for integrated GBV and SRH services.
Provision of psychosocial support, clinical management of rape, legal counselling, cash assistance, dignity kits, and vocational training.
Capacity-building for government authorities, local partners, and community structures.
Community engagement activities including awareness sessions, EMAP, and protection monitoring.
Emergency preparedness planning and rapid response readiness.
Expected Outcomes:
Survivors and at-risk individuals access timely, lifesaving, and coordinated GBV and SRH services.
Strengthened local and government capacity to prevent and respond to GBV.
Enhanced community resilience and economic empowerment, contributing to safer, more equitable environments.
Rationale: The protracted conflicts and insecurity in Borno, Katsina, and Zamfara have led to widespread GBV and limited access to essential services. Funding from FCDO will enable a coordinated, evidence-based, and sustainable response that addresses both immediate lifesaving needs and systemic protection gaps.

title.narrative: The project aims to improve access to lifesaving, coordinated GBV and SRH services for survivors and at-risk individuals in Northeast and Northwest Nigeria, while strengthening local initiatives for preventing and responding to GBV. It focuses on key outcomes : 1) Strengthening access to quality, lifesaving, and well-coordinated GBV and SRH services, 2) Enhancing survivor-centered services and implementing risk mitigation measures in humanitarian settings, and 3) Building community resilience through strengthening local systems and women led institutions to prevent and respond to GBV. To achieve these outcomes, the project will establish survivor-centered models, like one-stop centers integrating GBV, SRH, PSS and legal counselling. Targeted interventions include GBV Case Management, Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), vocational training, support fees for legal aid, provision of dignity kits, and emergency reproductive health kits. Capacity-building for local partners (BOWDI, SWODEN and RHHF) will ensure culturally relevant and sustainable delivery service while fostering community ownership. In the medium to long term, the project will contribute to a more resilient, gender-equal environment where women and girls have increased access to services, and local systems are equipped to prevent and respond to GBV independently.
